desc:
Product catalog data cleanup for recommendations fixes the tags, collections and variants that suggestion tools depend on. Ecom Swift LLC audits your catalog, repairs it with a consistent system and leaves you a guide for adding new products.

## Why suggestions depend on catalog data

A recommendation tool cannot see what a product is. It reads your tags, collections, titles, types and variants, then guesses what belongs together. If a leather wallet carries the tag "gift" and a phone case carries "Gifts", the tool treats them as unrelated.

Poor data leads to odd results: a winter coat shown beside a swimsuit, duplicates of the same item, or a related block that is empty because nothing shares a tag. Shoppers notice, and they stop trusting every suggestion on the store.

## Why does catalog data affect product suggestions?

Catalog data affects product suggestions because rules and learning models both start from the same inputs: collections, tags, product types, prices and variants. When those inputs are consistent, a rule such as "same collection, similar price" returns sensible items. When they are mixed, the same rule returns noise.

Good data also makes everything else easier. Search, filters, feeds, emails and reports all read the same fields, so one cleanup helps several parts of the store at once.

## What clean data does for results

Clean data lets suggestions look intentional. Shoppers see items that match what they are viewing, which keeps them browsing and makes add to cart clicks more likely. Your own team also spends less time fixing odd results by hand.

Be realistic about the limits. Cleanup does not create demand, and a tidy catalog does not promise more sales. It removes a common cause of weak suggestions, so any tool you use can perform at its best.

## What a well-organized catalog includes

- One naming pattern for product titles.
- A short, agreed list of tags with a clear meaning for each.
- Collections that each have one purpose, without overlaps.
- Product types that match how shoppers describe items.
- Attributes such as material, color family or fit, stored consistently.
- Variant names that follow one format, such as size labels.
- Duplicate or near duplicate products flagged for review.
- Image alt text that describes the product.
- A short guide so new products follow the same rules.

## How we do the work

First we take a backup of your product data, so every change can be reversed. We then audit the catalog in a spreadsheet, listing missing tags, mixed collections, odd titles and unclear variants. You see the findings and agree the tag system before we edit anything.

After approval we apply the fixes in your store admin, either by hand or in bulk through a spreadsheet import. We tidy and rename collections, make variant names consistent and flag duplicates for you to decide on. Basic covers a first group of products. Standard widens the cleanup and adds a single tag system. Premium adds attributes, variant cleanup, a data guide and a period of follow up fixes.

We do not rewrite your product descriptions as part of this service, and we leave your product pages' design alone.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide on tag names once and write them down.
- Keep one idea per collection.
- Use the same size and color labels everywhere.
- Export a backup before any bulk edit.
- Check suggestions again after the cleanup.

**Avoid:**
- Using several tags for the same idea.
- Putting every product in a catch all collection.
- Deleting duplicates without checking orders and links.
- Letting each team member invent new tags.
- Editing live products without a backup.

## Who this is for

This service suits stores that grew quickly and now have mixed tags from several people or suppliers. It also suits owners who imported products from a marketplace or a supplier file and never tidied the result. If you plan to add a recommendation tool soon, cleaning first means the tool starts with better material.

## What we need from you

Share a product export or give us access to your store admin as a collaborator or staff user. Tell us your main product groups, any words your customers use and any collections you want to keep. We never need your password. We send the audit findings before making changes, and you approve the tag system first.
